findings.claim: pkg/server/wire.go (lines 374-375) still registers anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore and binds AnonStore. ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 parameter that no Wire provider supplies, and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService builds its own store instead of receiving AnonStore, so wire generation fails or the binding is dead.

verifier.reason: The dead-binding half of the claim holds; the wire-failure half is unlikely (reasoned from Wire's on-demand solving, not run). pkg/server/wire.go:374-375 still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds `AnonStore`, but `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now takes `db.DB` and builds its own store (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:36-43), and no other Wire provider consumes `AnonStore` or `*AnonDBStore`, so the unsatisfiable `int64` parameter (anonstore/database.go:52) is never resolved.

findings.claim: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0. Zero affected rows means the device does not exist or its updated_at falls outside the time window, not that the limit was reached.

verifier.reason: The code does return ErrDeviceLimitReached on zero affected rows (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95-96), but updateDevice has a single caller that only runs once count >= deviceLimit (database.go:115-116). In that context an unmatched device is a new or expired one that cannot be added because the limit is reached, so the error is accurate.

findings.claim: Using RowsAffected()==0 to signal ErrDeviceLimitReached can misfire on MySQL. MySQL reports 0 rows affected when a row matches but its values are unchanged, for example the same updated_at after second-precision truncation, so existing devices at the limit can be denied.

verifier.reason: Grafana's MySQL DSN is built with `clientFoundRows=true` (pkg/services/sqlstore/sqlstore.go:287), so `RowsAffected()` at pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:90-96 returns matched rows, not changed rows, and an existing device with unchanged values still yields 1. Only the raw `connection_string` override, commented as a special case for integration tests (sqlstore.go:275-277), bypasses this flag.

findings.claim: The anonymousDeviceLimit field on the GrafanaBootConfig class is initialized to undefined without a type annotation, so TypeScript infers type undefined instead of number | undefined. The value cannot be read as a number even though the backend sends an int64.

verifier.reason: The field is declared as `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no annotation at packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 (the class lives there, not in grafana-data), and root tsconfig.json:8 sets `strict: true`, so its type is inferred as `undefined` rather than the interface's `number | undefined` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200). The effect is type-level only: `merge(this, defaults, options)` at config.ts:191 still assigns the backend number at runtime, and nothing in the frontend reads the field yet.

findings.claim: The new [auth.anonymous] device_limit config key is not added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or docs/sources/administration/configuration.md. Nothing documents that 0 means unlimited.

verifier.reason: The patch reads the new key at pkg/setting/setting.go:1654 (`anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)`), but it touches no file under conf/ or docs/, and a search for `device_limit` across conf/ and docs/ finds nothing. The 0-means-unlimited behaviour is only implicit in the `if s.deviceLimit > 0` check in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go.

findings.claim: The device limit tests do not verify that an already-known device can still be updated or refreshed when the limit is reached. They also do not cover other limit cases or the service/cache path, and impl_test.go only uses limit 0.

verifier.reason: The only limit test is `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-70), which uses limit 1 and asserts only that a new device is rejected; it never re-submits the existing device to exercise the successful `updateDevice` path. Both service tests in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl_test.go:117 and :152 pass `setting.NewCfg()`, so `AnonymousDeviceLimit` is 0 and the limit branch is never reached through `TagDevice` or the local cache.

findings.claim: tagDeviceUI writes the device ID to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and does not evict it on ErrDeviceLimitReached. Later requests from a rejected device hit the cache, TagDevice returns nil, and the device bypasses the limit until the cache entry expires.

verifier.reason: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:83-87 returns nil on a cache hit and sets the key before CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93), with no eviction when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached (anonstore/database.go:96). Only the first request from an over-limit device is rejected in client.go:44-46; later ones get nil from TagDevice and authenticate as anonymous until the 29-minute cache TTL (impl.go:42) expires.

findings.claim: The test device struct is missing the CreatedAt field.

verifier.reason: The new test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` builds its `Device` literal at pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:55-60 without `CreatedAt`, so the zero time is inserted via database.go:120-121. The pre-existing tests in the same file (lines 19-24, 77-82) omit it in the same way and the new test's assertion does not depend on it.

findings.claim: anonymousDeviceLimit is added to the public GrafanaConfig interface and the frontend settings DTO, but nothing in public/ or packages/ reads it. Adding a required member to a published interface also affects implementers.

verifier.reason: The patch adds a required `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` to GrafanaConfig (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200) and to the DTO (pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195, set at pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198); the only other frontend occurrence is the default in packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97, and nothing in public/ or packages/ reads it. The sole in-repo implementer, GrafanaBootConfig (packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:37), was updated, so only external implementers are affected.

findings.claim: The device limit is exposed in frontend settings to all clients, including unauthenticated anonymous ones.

verifier.reason: pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198 copies hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit into the frontend settings DTO with no signed-in check, and that DTO is served unauthenticated via LoginView (pkg/api/api.go:76 -> pkg/api/login.go:101 setIndexViewData -> pkg/api/index.go:29) and to anonymous sessions on index pages. The value is only a configured cap sitting next to the already-public anonymousEnabled flag, so the disclosure is low-sensitivity.

findings.claim: args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...) mutates the captured slice inside the WithDbSession callback. On a SQLite 'database locked' retry, the query is prepended twice and Exec fails.

verifier.reason: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:84 reassigns the captured `args` inside the callback, and pkg/services/sqlstore/session.go:90 re-invokes that same callback on SQLite ErrLocked/ErrBusy, so a second attempt passes [query, query, 6 args] to Exec, giving 7 bind values for 6 placeholders. It only triggers when `query_retries` is 2 or more (default is 0 in conf/defaults.ini:161), and the same pattern already exists at database.go:150.

findings.claim: CountDevices and the subsequent insert/update in CreateOrUpdateDevice run in separate sessions without a transaction or lock. Concurrent requests or HA instances can all observe count < limit and insert devices beyond the limit.

verifier.reason: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:109-117 the limit check calls CountDevices (its own WithDbSession, lines 158-166), and the upsert then runs in a separate WithDbSession at lines 149-153 with no transaction, mutex or server lock around the pair. Concurrent requests or HA instances can each read count < limit and each insert a new device, overshooting the limit.

findings.claim: The 30-day device window is defined in three places: anonymousDeviceExpiration in anonstore/database.go and api/api.go, and thirtyDays in impl.go. If one drifts, the enforced count, device listing and usage stats will disagree.

verifier.reason: The same `30 * 24 * time.Hour` window is declared three times: `anonymousDeviceExpiration` at pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:16 (limit enforcement, lines 81 and 110), `anonymousDeviceExpiration` at pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go:18 (device listing, line 71), and `thirtyDays` at pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:25 (device count, line 70). All three are equal today, so the disagreement is only a future drift risk.

findings.claim: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and panic recovery to a synchronous call on the anonymous auth path. This adds DB write latency to requests, removes panic recovery, and ties the write to the request context.

verifier.reason: The patch removes the `go func()` with `recover()` and the 2-minute `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag)`, and `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44` now calls `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inline in `Authenticate` with the request context. The write at `impl.go:93` (plus a `CountDevices` query when a limit is set, `anonstore/database.go`) therefore runs on the request path, though the local cache at `impl.go:83-87` limits it to roughly once per device per 29 minutes.

findings.claim: The new TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit lacks the testing.Short() skip guard.

verifier.reason: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-70 adds TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit, which goes straight to db.InitTestDB(t) at line 52 with no `if testing.Short() { t.Skip(...) }` guard. The neighbouring TestIntegration* tests in the same file (lines 14 and 72) also lack the guard, so the new test follows the existing local pattern.

findings.claim: The device-limit time window is computed inconsistently. CountDevices uses time.Now().UTC(), while the upsert uses device.UpdatedAt and device.UpdatedAt.Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as its bounds.

verifier.reason: The limit check counts devices in a window anchored on time.Now().UTC() (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110), while the fallback updateDevice anchors its BETWEEN bounds on device.UpdatedAt.UTC() (database.go:80-81; upper bound is actually UpdatedAt+1min, and it is the plain UPDATE, not the upsert). The only production caller sets UpdatedAt to time.Now() (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:141), so the two windows differ by a negligible amount in practice.

findings.claim: When TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, Authenticate in client.go fails, so anonymous authentication is blocked entirely rather than only device tracking being capped.

verifier.reason: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-47 now calls TagDevice synchronously and returns `nil, err` on `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which propagates from database.go:96 via impl.go:147, so a new device over the limit fails anonymous authentication. The explicit `errors.Is` branch looks deliberate, it applies only when `device_limit` > 0 and the request carries `X-Grafana-Device-Id`, and because impl.go:87 sets the local cache before the store call, repeat requests from the same device then pass.

findings.claim: ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain fmt.Errorf value rather than an errutil error. It is logged at Warn on every rejected request, and the client gets a generic 401 with no device-limit message.

verifier.reason: `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is a plain `fmt.Errorf` value (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:18), so `errorLogFunc` finds no `errutil.Error` and logs at Warn (pkg/services/authn/authnimpl/service.go:230, 356-364). `writeErrOrFallback` likewise falls back to a bare 401 "Unauthorized" for API requests (pkg/middleware/auth.go:39, pkg/services/contexthandler/model/model.go:116-117); non-API requests are redirected to /login instead, also with no device-limit message.

findings.claim: The doc comment says 'updated between the given times', but the function takes no time arguments; the window is derived from device.UpdatedAt.

verifier.reason: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:72-73 documents updateDevice as updating a device 'updated between the given times', but its signature is (ctx, device *Device) with no time parameters; the BETWEEN bounds are computed from device.UpdatedAt minus anonymousDeviceExpiration and plus one minute (lines ~80-82).

findings.claim: Clients that omit X-Grafana-Device-Id or send an unparsable IP are never counted but still authenticate as anonymous, so the limit can be bypassed by dropping the header.

verifier.reason: TagDevice returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is empty (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:119-122) or the IP fails to parse (impl.go:124-129), before the limit check in CreateOrUpdateDevice is ever reached. Authenticate only rejects on ErrDeviceLimitReached and otherwise returns the anonymous identity (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-58), so such requests bypass the limit.
